chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Bishr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came, and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said, instead of “a qāmah and two qāmahs,” “a cubit and two cubits.”

key_terms.الْقَامَةِ: a qāmah; a unit mentioned for determining prayer time
key_terms.الْقَامَتَيْنِ: two qāmahs; a doubled measure in the timing expression
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel mentioned in the report
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a cubit; an alternative unit of measure used in this version
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْنِ: two cubits; the doubled form of the alternative measure
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: the like of it; referring to the previously mentioned report or wording

ai.seo_question: What wording is reported for the prayer-time measurement in the hadith of Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a variant wording concerning the measurement used in describing the beginning of the times of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr. Instead of the expression “one qāmah and two qāmahs,” it uses “one cubit and two cubits,” which is relevant to prayer-time rulings in fiqh.
